- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price drops, model underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 72, true price often drops below 70; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, model overfits recent volatility; use 10-day rolling average of true price to anchor forecast if sentiment is ambiguous or mixed.  
- When sentiment is uniformly low (≤ 0.33) and price is stable, model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% upward bias to avoid missing early recovery.
